gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 2?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from multiple meteorological models indicate a daily maximum near 25°C in Munich on September 2, driven by mild westerly flow, persistent cloud cover limiting solar insolation, and surface temperatures peaking in the mid-afternoon before cooling. This aligns with the historical September average high of around 22°C and recent observational trends showing no anomalous warming. Trader consensus at 100% for 25°C reflects the tight clustering of model outputs and official guidance, with minimal variance expected from steering patterns or humidity. A realistic challenge could arise from localized clear-sky breaks enhancing radiative heating or an official station reading slightly above threshold due to urban heat effects, though such deviations remain low-probability given the stable synoptic setup.

Low precipitation probabilities (under 10–30% in most runs) and absence of strong frontal systems reduce the chance of rapid cooling from cloud cover or rain. Historical context reinforces the range: while the all-time September 3 record stands at 30.5°C, recent analogs cluster near 24–26°C under similar synoptic patterns.

Traders appear to be pricing in the tight spread across operational models (DWD, GFS, and others), with limited upside risk from unexpected clear skies or downside from increased cloudiness. Real-time station data and updated model runs through the afternoon will provide the final confirmation as the market resolves.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the Met Office and numerical weather prediction models position 22–23°C as the most probable range for London's maximum temperature on September 4, 2026.** 

A shift to westerly flow, increased cloud cover, and scattered showers or drizzle are limiting daytime solar heating after warmer conditions on September 3. Ensemble guidance from the ECMWF and GFS shows surface highs constrained by these factors, with afternoon temperatures peaking near 21–23°C amid moderate winds. Historical September climatology for London supports maxima in this band when Atlantic air masses dominate. 

Market-implied probabilities align closely with this model consensus, reflecting trader assessment of the narrow uncertainty window before resolution. Minor model spread on shower timing or brief cloud breaks could still nudge the exact peak within the 21–24°C band.

National Weather Service preliminary climatological reports and multiple real-time networks (including Central Park-area stations) recorded a daily maximum consistent with 74°F, aligning precisely with the leading market outcome.

This positioning rests on verified observational data rather than forecasts. Only an unexpected post-event revision to the official maximum—highly improbable given multiple corroborating sources—or a non-standard resolution criterion would meaningfully alter the result. The market's near-certainty captures the skin-in-the-game assessment of these stable, post-event measurements.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official meteorological observations from Munich-area stations, including standard DWD and Nymphenburg records, recorded a daily maximum of 25°C on September 2, 2026.** This value aligns with real-time surface measurements under partly cloudy to overcast conditions, light westerly winds, and stable high pressure near 1020 hPa, which limited daytime heating despite some morning sun. Multiple independent forecasts converged on highs of 23–26°C, and post-event summaries confirm the peak fell squarely at the 25°C threshold rather than pushing higher.

Trader consensus at near-100% for 25°C (versus negligible odds for 27°C) reflects the strength of these verified observations over any residual model spread. Historical September 2 averages near 22°C and the absence of strong advection or clear-sky amplification further supported this outcome.

A realistic challenge would require an official data revision—such as a station-specific correction, quality-control adjustment, or use of an alternate measurement site—which remains possible but rare once preliminary reports stabilize.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service observations from Central Park recorded a maximum of 71°F on September 2 under persistent overcast skies, light rain, and easterly flow that suppressed daytime heating well below the 80–81°F climatological normal. Model guidance and surface analyses indicated limited insolation and a stable marine-influenced air mass kept afternoon readings capped near 70–72°F, aligning with the market’s overwhelming 99.7% implied probability for the 74–75°F bin once preliminary data confirmed the outcome. A late-model shift toward clearer skies or stronger southerly advection could have pushed readings 4–6°F higher, but no such development materialized before resolution criteria were met.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Historical September baselines for Munich average 20–22°C, making this outlier warmth notable. Updated high-resolution model guidance and official DWD forecasts issued overnight will likely refine the final outcome before markets close.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office forecasts and supporting model guidance indicate a likely maximum of 22–23°C in London on September 5 under partly cloudy skies and light westerly winds, with afternoon peaks supported by modest insolation and a stable high-pressure influence. Ensemble spreads from ECMWF and GFS runs introduce realistic variability of ±2–3°C tied to subtle differences in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing, which explains the market’s even distribution of implied probabilities across 20–25°C. Dry conditions and seasonal norms for early September further constrain extremes, though any late-day clearing or wind shift could nudge the daily high toward the upper or lower end of that range ahead of final observations.

This setup favors modest daytime warming from autumnal insolation levels without strong advection or prolonged clear-sky heating, keeping values near the early-September climatological mean. Minor forecast spread arises from uncertainties in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing, which could nudge the peak by 1°C either way, while the overall pattern shows low risk of exceeding 24°C or falling below 21°C. Trader sentiment aligns closely with these near-term official guidance updates.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and ensemble model guidance points to a post-frontal high-pressure ridge over the Northeast, with northerly flow advecting cooler, drier air into the NYC area by September 5. This setup favors mostly sunny skies and daytime highs clustering in the upper 70s to low 80s, consistent with the market’s leading 80-81 °F bin. Earlier in the week, southwesterly flow and higher dew points supported mid-80s readings before a cold front moderated temperatures. Model spread remains modest, centered on 78–81 °F, though minor timing differences in the ridge’s arrival or residual cloud cover could shift the daily maximum by a degree or two. Traders appear to be weighting the consensus forecast while discounting outlier warmer scenarios given the established northerly steering pattern.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Morning observations near 70°F and afternoon model runs holding steady in the low-to-mid 80s reinforce the current market-implied odds, with limited upside from stronger heating given cloud cover and moisture. Updated forecasts later today could refine exact maxima before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble and deterministic model runs from the GFS, ECMWF, and UK Met Office show London under building high pressure on September 5, with light westerly flow and limited cloud cover supporting a maximum temperature centered on 21–23 °C. Surface observations and 10-day guidance place the most likely peak near 22–23 °C, consistent with the market’s heaviest volume on those outcomes. A modest warm bias in some GFS members keeps the slim 24 °C probability live, while cooler solutions remain under 10 % given the stable ridge. Updated model cycles and the next Met Office briefing are the key near-term catalysts that could shift implied probabilities before resolution.

**Forecast consensus from the National Weather Service and regional models positions mid-80s readings as the most likely outcome for New York City's highest temperature today.** 

Official area forecast matrices and local observations indicate a high in the 83–86°F range under partly sunny skies with southwest winds of 5–10 mph and 40% storm chances that are unlikely to suppress peak readings. This exceeds the September 3 climatological average high of roughly 80°F at Central Park while remaining well below historical extremes near 99°F. Morning observations near 70°F with high humidity and building clouds support continued warming into the afternoon before any showers develop. Trader-implied probabilities cluster on the 84–87°F bins because ensemble guidance shows limited downside risk from clouds or precipitation and modest upside potential if breaks of sun allow brief spikes. Updated model runs and real-time surface observations through midday will refine the exact peak before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models project a September 5 high near 25–26°C in Tokyo under persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly flow associated with a frontal system and upstream low-pressure influences. This pattern limits solar heating and advects cooler maritime air, keeping daytime maxima well below the late-summer climatological average of ~29°C. Trader consensus clusters on 25°C (32.5%) and 26°C (31.0%) because these align with the narrow range of guidance; differentiation among 24–27°C hinges on small differences in cloud thickness, any brief afternoon breaks in rain, exact wind direction, and boundary-layer mixing within model runs. Updated JMA guidance and observational trends through September 4 will further refine the expected maximum.

This aligns with typical early-September climatology, where London highs average near 19–20°C, though the current pattern sits slightly above baseline without reaching anomalous warmth. A northerly flow behind a frontal passage is expected to deliver sunny skies and drier air after midweek warmth and humidity, with highs near or slightly above the late-summer climatological average of roughly 80°F. Model consensus and current guidance cluster tightly around 78–80°F, with limited spread arising mainly from exact wind speeds, boundary-layer mixing, and the precise location of the official Central Park observation. 

Traders are therefore weighting the two central outcomes most heavily because small forecast adjustments—such as a degree or two of additional warming from clearer skies or slightly lighter winds—can shift the daily maximum across the 80°F threshold, while downside risks remain modest given the established post-frontal regime. Upcoming model runs and short-range updates will be the key near-term drivers of any further movement in these probabilities.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model runs from the Met Office, ECMWF, and GFS show a frontal boundary approaching London, increasing cloud cover and introducing light rain or drizzle that limits daytime heating after Thursday’s warmer conditions. This setup supports maximum temperatures clustering in the 21–23°C range, with ensemble guidance placing the most likely outcome near 22°C under moderate southwesterly winds. Historical September baselines and current pressure trends reinforce modest cooling rather than sharp drops or spikes. Traders weigh these signals against potential model spread on exact timing of clearance, keeping 21–23°C as the dominant implied probabilities ahead of final observational data.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models project a September 5 high near 25–26°C in Tokyo under persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly flow associated with a frontal system and upstream low-pressure influences. This pattern limits solar heating and advects cooler maritime air, keeping daytime maxima well below the late-summer climatological average of ~29°C. Trader consensus clusters on 25°C (32.5%) and 26°C (31.0%) because these align with the narrow range of guidance; differentiation among 24–27°C hinges on small differences in cloud thickness, any brief afternoon breaks in rain, exact wind direction, and boundary-layer mixing within model runs. Updated JMA guidance and observational trends through September 4 will further refine the expected maximum.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Met Office and other agencies indicate a daytime high of 25–27°C across London on September 3, 2026, under partly cloudy skies with westerly winds of 10–15 mph and moderate humidity. This positions 26°C as the dominant outcome, reflecting a mild Atlantic air mass typical for early September that limits daytime warming while preventing cooler northerly flow. Model consensus shows stable conditions without strong high pressure or heat advection that would push temperatures to 28°C or above, or significant cloud and rain that would cap them below 25°C. Traders’ heavy weighting toward 26°C aligns with these real-time observations and short-range guidance, with only modest probability assigned to a one-degree variance based on minor timing shifts in cloud cover or wind.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on September 4, 2026, centers on 21–23°C, reflecting model consensus for a cooler, fresher day after warmer conditions on the 3rd.**

Official guidance from the Met Office and BBC Weather highlights an incoming Atlantic weather front bringing increased cloud cover, patchy drizzle or light rain, and moderate westerly winds that limit daytime heating. This synoptic setup favors maximum temperatures several degrees below the prior day's potential peaks near 27°C, with reduced solar insolation and advection of cooler maritime air keeping readings in the low-to-mid 20s Celsius.

Ensemble forecasts show tight clustering around 21–23°C as the most probable range, consistent with early September climatology when unsettled patterns often cap highs despite occasional warmer intrusions. Higher outcomes above 24°C carry low implied probability due to the expected cloud and wind effects, while sub-20°C scenarios remain unlikely absent stronger cooling. Updated model runs and Met Office briefings on frontal timing will be key near-term catalysts for any shifts in these market-implied odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Met Office and numerical weather models indicate a daytime maximum near 25–26°C across London on September 3, 2026, under mostly cloudy skies with southwesterly winds of 12–15 mph and minimal precipitation risk. This consensus aligns with late-summer climatology for the region, where highs typically reach the mid-20s before cooling later in the month. Trader positioning at 26°C reflects the tight clustering of model guidance and observed afternoon temperatures approaching that threshold. A realistic shift away from this outcome would require either greater-than-expected cloud cover suppressing insolation or clearer conditions allowing a brief spike above 27°C before official verification at representative stations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the Met Office and ensemble models point to a mostly cloudy Friday with light rain or drizzle possible early, moderating temperatures under westerly flow and yielding a daytime high near 21–22°C in London. This aligns with the market’s leading implied probabilities for those exact outcomes, as traders weigh the latest GFS and regional guidance against historical September averages around 19–20°C. Persistent cloud cover and fresh Atlantic air limit daytime warming potential compared to the warmer, sunnier conditions expected later in the weekend, while any model shift toward clearer skies or stronger southerly flow could push readings toward 23°C. The next updated Met Office briefing and 00Z–12Z model runs tomorrow morning represent the key data releases likely to refine these probabilities before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance position 22–23°C as the most probable range for London’s maximum temperature on September 5, 2026.** The Met Office forecasts a high of 23°C under clearing skies and light westerly winds after Friday’s rain, with hourly readings peaking near that value. Other sources, including ECMWF-influenced and GFS-based outputs, cluster between 21–23°C, reflecting a stable high-pressure ridge and seasonal early-September climatology that limits stronger warming.

Market-implied odds (23°C at 51.5%, 22°C at 36%) closely track this consensus, while the modest 10% probability on 24°C captures residual uncertainty in model spread and local urban heat effects. Recent shifts—such as the transition from Thursday’s warmer, more humid conditions (25–27°C) to fresher northwesterly flow—have narrowed expectations downward, reinforcing trader focus on the narrow 22–23°C band ahead of final model runs on September 4.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Mild Atlantic air advection, combined with limited daytime heating from broken cloud cover and light winds, has kept temperatures from exceeding this level, consistent with early September climatology for the region where highs typically range 18–22°C but can reach the mid-20s during settled spells. This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models indicate persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly flow over Tokyo on September 5, limiting solar heating and capping daytime highs near 25–26°C. High humidity and overnight rain further moderate surface temperatures by enhancing evaporative cooling and reducing boundary-layer mixing. Ensemble spreads show limited upside potential above 27°C without a sharp reduction in cloudiness, while downside risk to 24°C or below remains if heavier precipitation arrives earlier. Trader consensus around the 25–26°C outcomes reflects this narrow range of likely maxima, with differentiation driven by subtle variations in model timing of showers and shortwave radiation. Updated high-resolution runs and morning observations will provide the next key inputs before resolution.
